recent_posts.title: SumoDB in Neo4j: Graph Analytics in Snowflake — Part 2
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on walkthrough of using Neo4j Graph Analytics for Snowflake to analyze Grand Sumo wrestling data. Covers installing the Neo4j Graph Analytics app from the Snowflake Marketplace, setting up permissions, preparing CSV data as Snowflake tables, and running the Louvain Community Detection algorithm on bout data from the Kyushu Basho 2025. The results show that the algorithm successfully infers rikishi rank groupings purely from bout pairing relationships, without any explicit rank data provided.

recent_posts.title: Using amnesia prompts to stop GraphRAG agents from hallucinating citations
recent_posts.summary: A developer building a GraphRAG system (Senegraph) for Stoic philosophy discovered that LLM agents with extensive domain knowledge in their training data would skip tool calls and hallucinate citations instead. Despite strong instructional prompts demanding tool use, the Seneca agent fabricated quotes 50%+ of the time. The breakthrough came from reframing the agent's identity: instead of telling it 'you must search,' the system prompt told it 'your memory is unreliable — you have amnesia.' This situational framing dropped fabrication to zero on first turns, because it reframes an actual LLM limitation as an intrinsic identity trait the agent cannot reason away. The post also covers a frontend parser that catches any fabricated citations and triggers a retry, ensuring users only ever see graph-backed quotes.

recent_posts.title: Graph Intelligence: Network Intrusion Detection with Neo4j and Snowflake
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step walkthrough of building a network intrusion detection system using Neo4j Graph Analytics for Snowflake. The pipeline combines K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) to construct a similarity graph from IoT network flow data and GraphSAGE for supervised node classification to detect attacks (DDoS, DoS, Reconnaissance, Theft). All computation runs inside Snowflake via Snowpark Container Services on CPU and GPU instances, keeping data within the Snowflake enclave. The implementation reproduces results from an academic paper, achieving a weighted F1-score of 0.985 and macro-F1 of 0.811 on a 600K-node IoT dataset.

recent_posts.title: Migrate from apoc.periodic.iterate to CALL IN TRANSACTIONS in Neo4j
recent_posts.summary: Neo4j's APOC plugin procedure `apoc.periodic.iterate` is being superseded by native Cypher's `CALL { … } IN TRANSACTIONS` (CIT). CIT offers several advantages: proper memory tracking that prevents OOM crashes, better readability and IDE tooling support, full query planning visibility via EXPLAIN, accurate query statistics, no need for entity rebinding (fetching nodes twice), concurrent transaction support, and an ON ERROR RETRY option added in Neo4j 2025.03. APOC Core is now in maintenance mode with no new features planned, making migration to CIT the recommended path for all bulk transactional operations.

recent_posts.title: Building a Global HR Policy Assistant with GraphRAG: A Beginner’s Guide
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to building a global HR policy assistant using GraphRAG and Neo4j. The core technique introduced is 'classifier nodes' (e.g., BenefitType, BenefitCategory) that connect extracted entities into a navigable knowledge graph instead of isolated document fragments. The guide covers a custom multi-phase pipeline: PDF ingestion, text chunking, embedding, two-phase LLM entity extraction (document-level and chunk-level), entity resolution, index creation, and post-processing to create classifier nodes. It then shows how to deploy a Neo4j Aura Agent on top of the graph to answer employee HR questions using a combination of vector similarity search and graph traversal. Example queries demonstrate how the agent handles contextual questions about leave entitlements and medical insurance across countries and organizational bands.

recent_posts.title: Using Agents to Secure Satellites’ Supply Chain Systems
recent_posts.summary: A cybersecurity professional presents a threat modelling exercise for satellite supply chain systems using a Neo4j knowledge graph. By mapping relationships between satellites, components, vulnerabilities, suppliers, ground stations, users, and roles, the graph reveals attack propagation paths that flat data structures cannot. The project was demonstrated at ESA's AI STAR Symposium and extended with a Neo4j Aura Agent that lets security analysts query the graph in plain language without writing Cypher. The post highlights the real-world risk of satellite cyberattacks, citing Japan's 2024 space agency breach and rising software supply chain attack rates, and provides a basic guide for replicating the approach.

recent_posts.title: Pattern Matching: Turning Connected Data Into Actionable Intelligence
recent_posts.summary: Graph databases fundamentally change how pattern matching works by storing relationships as first-class citizens rather than reconstructing them via joins. Using Neo4j and Cypher, complex structural queries like circular payment detection, shortest path routing, blast radius impact analysis, and multi-hop dependency chains can be expressed declaratively and executed in seconds versus minutes in SQL. Four real-world patterns are demonstrated with Cypher code: circular fraud rings (3-10 hops), supply chain shortest paths, server failure blast radius traversal, and gene-disease-drug dependency chains. Performance best practices cover bounded variable-length patterns, index usage, and when graph databases are not the right tool (flat aggregations, key-value lookups, time-series data).

recent_posts.title: Neo4j and the Data Ecosystem
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive overview of Neo4j's data integration connectors and ecosystem partnerships, written by the PM for the Connectors team. Covers connectors for AWS Glue, Apache Kafka, Apache Spark, Confluent, Databricks, Google Dataflow/BigQuery, Snowflake, and Microsoft Fabric. Also details toolkit components including the Neo4j JDBC v6 driver with SQL2Cypher translation, Import Spec, Change Data Capture, and the Java Driver. Notable highlights include a coming Unity Catalogue connector for Databricks, GA of Graph Intelligence for Microsoft Fabric, and a Snowflake AI agent for graph analytics. Each connector entry includes availability links and recommended resources.

recent_posts.title: Structured AI with Neo4j
recent_posts.summary: Neo4j 2026.02.0 introduces a new `ai.text.structuredCompletion` Cypher procedure that returns AI-generated output conforming to a user-defined JSON schema. The post demonstrates this with a practical dinner planner app: a structured recipe is generated via OpenAI using user preferences, allergies, and recent meals, then stored as a graph with ingredient nodes, vector embeddings, and relationships. The resulting graph enables weekly dinner planning, shopping list generation, and even vector-similarity-based user matching. The post also covers the new CYPHER 25 vector search syntax and notes limitations like unit normalization in shopping lists.

recent_posts.title: Context Graphs and AI Memory Across the Globe
recent_posts.summary: Two simultaneous meetups in Berlin and San Francisco independently converged on the same architectural conclusion: agentic AI systems need context graphs as a structured memory layer. A context graph combines a knowledge graph with decision traces, provenance, and temporal validity, enabling agents to reason across workflows in an auditable way. Speakers emphasized that building context graphs is fundamentally a knowledge management problem, not just an engineering one, requiring knowledge elicitation and formal ontologies before any persistence layer. Key production principles included resolving data contradictions at build time and designing governance with full delegation chains from the start. The emerging consensus is that context graphs will become standard infrastructure in AI-capable software, analogous to unit tests.
